bio.short: I hold product management and product design as one job, doing it today at Bibel TV. I have done the same at ChurchDesk and, briefly, as interim Head of Product at Ninox. I ship AI work rather than talk about it, and I bring marketplace and e-commerce experience from Spreadshirt.
bio.long:
At Bibel TV I am product manager and product owner for the app redesign, alongside leading product design across iOS, Android, web and connected TV — the redesign is the purpose of the engagement, not a duty attached to it. I redesigned the entry point to an AI feature and usage rose 153% on iOS and 85% on Android, four-week averages before and after. I also shipped a production support copilot and an end-to-end AI fundraising pipeline, analysis through prompt engineering to a working prototype, solo.

At ChurchDesk I held product management for the main platform alongside all product design, across six European markets. When a single church asked for a funeral-booking feature, I reframed it into a platform capability serving both the parishes and the funeral homes booking through it — the closest analogue in my record to a two-sided product decision, though not an advertising or monetisation one. It shipped in two months, cut coordination time 70%, reached 90% acceptance, and rolled out to the whole customer base.

Earlier, at Ninox, I led two functions at once for four months as interim Head of Product — product design and UX writing, plus three product managers and one data scientist — and at Spreadshirt I led the nine-month redesign of a dual-sided marketplace serving ~5,000 business sellers and hundreds of thousands of consumers. I work in German natively and English at C2.

context.role: Senior Product Manager, Advertising (fixed-term, maternity cover)

Never claim advertising or monetisation-product experience directly; the ChurchDesk analogue is named once, clearly scoped as an analogue.
